premise: Daily P&L for the EUR bond book fell by 1.2M on 2026-09-15.
good: Re-run the daily P&L query for the EUR bond book for 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-15; if the change is not within 0.1M of -1.2M, the premise is false.
bad: If the P&L numbers turn out to be different, the premise would be wrong.

premise: The drop was driven by the EUR/USD rate moving from 1.10 to 1.07.
good: Recompute the book's P&L holding EUR/USD fixed at 1.10; if more than half of the 1.2M drop remains, FX was not the driver.
bad: A different explanation for the drop would show this is false.

premise: The positions table has one row per position per day.
good: Count rows grouped by position_id and date; any group with more than one row falsifies this.
bad: Checking the table more carefully could reveal problems.

premise: Trading volume on the exchange doubled after the fee cut.
good: Compare average daily volume in the 30 trading days before and after the fee cut in the exchange's published statistics; a ratio below 1.5 falsifies it.
bad: If volume didn't really go up that much, this would be false.

premise: The new onboarding flow raised day-7 retention.
good: Compare day-7 retention for users who signed up in the two weeks before and after launch; no increase outside the 95% confidence interval falsifies it.
bad: User feedback could show the onboarding flow didn't help.

premise: The Eiffel Tower was completed in 1889.
good: A primary record, such as the 1889 Exposition Universelle archives, dating completion to a different year would falsify it.
bad: Historians might disagree about this.

premise: The server outage began at 14:02 UTC.
good: Find the first 5xx error in the load balancer logs; if it is more than two minutes before or after 14:02 UTC, the premise is false.
bad: The logs might tell a different story.

premise: The price feed for bond XS123 was stale on 2026-09-15.
good: If the feed's last_update timestamp for XS123 on 2026-09-15 is later than 16:00 that day, the feed was not stale.
bad: Looking into the price feed would confirm or deny this.

premise: Customer churn is highest in the first month.
good: Compute monthly churn rates by tenure month for the last year's cohorts; if any later month's rate is higher than month one's, the premise is false.
bad: Churn could be highest at some other point.

premise: The vaccine reduced hospitalizations by 90% in the trial.
good: The trial's published hospitalization counts in the vaccine and placebo arms imply an efficacy below 80%; that would falsify it.
bad: Other studies might find something different.

premise: Most of the portfolio's risk comes from the energy sector.
good: Decompose portfolio variance by sector using the risk model; if energy contributes under 50%, the premise is false.
bad: The risk might actually be spread across other sectors.

premise: The bug was introduced in release 4.2.
good: Run the failing test against release 4.1; if it also fails there, the bug predates 4.2.
bad: The bug could have come from somewhere else.

premise: Rainfall in the region was below average this summer.
good: Compare total June-August rainfall at the regional weather stations against their 30-year average; a total at or above average falsifies it.
bad: Some people remember it being a wet summer.

premise: The model's accuracy on the test set is 91%.
good: Re-run the evaluation script on the frozen test set; any accuracy outside 90.5% to 91.5% falsifies it.
bad: The model might not be as accurate as reported.

premise: The duplicated trade inflated the book's notional by 50M.
good: Remove the duplicate trade ID from the positions table and recompute notional; if it drops by anything other than 50M, the premise is false.
bad: There may be other reasons the notional looks high.

premise: Sales in the Northeast region fell because of the storm.
good: Compare Northeast daily sales on storm-affected days with the same weekdays in the prior four weeks; if the drop is under 10% or appears on unaffected days too, the premise is false.
bad: It's possible the storm wasn't the real cause.

premise: The API's p99 latency exceeds 800 ms.
good: Pull the p99 latency from the monitoring dashboard for the last 24 hours; a value at or below 800 ms falsifies it.
bad: Latency could be better than it seems.

premise: The central bank raised rates by 25 basis points in March.
good: The central bank's March policy statement listing any change other than +25 bp falsifies it.
bad: Economists could interpret the March decision differently.

premise: The FX rate used for the 2026-09-15 revaluation was carried over from the prior day.
good: If the fx_rates row used for 2026-09-15 has an as_of date of 2026-09-15, the rate was not carried over.
bad: The rates might have been updated properly after all.

premise: Warehouse B handles most returns.
good: Count returns by receiving warehouse for the last quarter; if warehouse B has less than 50% of them, the premise is false.
bad: Other warehouses could be handling a lot of returns too.
